extracted.intended_audience: Patent examiners and patent practitioners (reissue applicants / patent prosecutors)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating whether claims in a reissue application impermissibly 'recapture' subject matter surrendered during prosecution of the original application under the recapture doctrine (35 U.S.C. 251). Provides definitions, a three-step test, examiner duties, examples, and guidance for determining surrender and material narrowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recapture (doctrine)
rubrics_metrics.description: A doctrine based upon the error requirement in 35 U.S.C. 251 that prevents a reissue applicant from claiming subject matter surrendered during the prosecution of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reissue will not be granted to “recapture” claimed subject matter which was surrendered in an application to obtain the original patent. The question of whether a reissue patent violates the rule against recapture of subject matter surrendered during original prosecution is a question of law (see cited cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening Claim (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue claim is “broadened” where at least one limitation of the patent claims is either completely eliminated or is only presented in a broader way in the reissue claim relative to the broadest patented claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reissue claim is not broadened in any respect as compared to the patent claims, the recapture analysis ends; there is no recapture. See MPEP § 1412.03 for further guidance as to the nature of a 'broadening claim.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Canceled Claim (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim canceled from the original application to obtain the patent for which reissue is being sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In recapture context, claims are considered canceled if they were deleted and not replaced or were replaced by other claims that are more specific than the canceled claims in at least one aspect in order to overcome a rejection in the original prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original Application (definition and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'original application' includes the prosecution record of the application that issued as the patent to be reissued and includes the patent family's entire prosecution history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrender may occur because of prosecution history of related applications; examiners must review the entire prosecution history (including related applications) when determining surrender. See MBO Laboratories v. Becton Dickinson and In re McDonald.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender Generating Limitation (SGL) / Surrendered Subject Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: An SGL is a 'limitation' presented, argued, or stated to make the claims patentable (in the original application) and 'generates' the surrender of claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An SGL can be created by presentation of new/amended claims or an argument/statement by applicant that a limitation defines the invention over the art. A patent owner is bound by arguments relied upon to overcome an art rejection even if the Office adopted a different rationale. An SGL can also be created to obviate rejections on other grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlooked Aspects (definition and exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims to separate inventions/embodiments/species that were not claimed in the original application prosecution (i.e., 'overlooked aspects').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlooked aspects are not a part of a recapture analysis. If a reissue claim adds an overlooked aspect (an invention never presented in the original application), that situation is treated separately (see MPEP §1412.01, subsection III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-step Test for Recapture (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recapture analysis is a three-step process: (1) determine whether and in what respect the reissue claims are broader than the original patent claims; (2) determine whether the broader aspects relate to subject matter surrendered in the original prosecution; (3) determine whether the reissue claims were materially narrowed in other respects so the claims may not have been enlarged and hence avoid recapture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If at any step the criterion for 'no recapture' is met, the analysis can stop per the notes in the test. The MPEP cites Clement, North American Container and related case law for this test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 — Is There Broadening? (examiner duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner must review each reissue claim for the presence of broadening as compared with the scope of the claims of the patent to be reissued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reissue claim is broadened if some limitation of the patent claims is no longer required in the reissue claim. If no broadening, analysis ends. Examiners should consult MPEP §1412.03 for types of broadening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A — Did Applicant Surrender Subject Matter?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether applicant surrendered any subject matter in the prosecution of the original application that became the patent to be reissued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an original patent claim limitation now omitted or broadened in the reissue was originally relied upon by applicant to make the claims allowable (by amendment or argument), the omitted limitation relates to surrendered subject matter. Examiner must review prosecution history (including rejections and applicant's arguments) to determine surrender. If applicant did not surrender subject matter, analysis ends — no recapture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2B — Does Broadening Relate to Surrendered Subject Matter?
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant did surrender subject matter, determine whether any of the broadening aspects of the reissue claims is in the area of the surrendered subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze all broadening aspects to see if omitted/broadened limitations are directed to limitations relied upon by applicant in the original application. If the reissue claims are broadened with respect to previously surrendered subject matter, recapture will be present regardless of unrelated narrowing limitations (Mostafazadeh).

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument Alone Can Create Surrender (precision required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surrender that forms basis for impermissible recapture can occur through applicant arguments alone (even without amendment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The argument relied upon must be specific as to the limitation relied upon rather than a general 'boilerplate' statement that the limitations of the claims define over the prior art. Boilerplate or general statements are insufficient to establish surrender. Examples of insufficient boilerplate are provided in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment Without Argument May Presumptively Show Surrender
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment adding a limitation to overcome a rejection (even without argument) can establish that the limitation was added to obviate the rejection and thus its later omission in reissue can be recapture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If limitation D was added in the original application in direct reply to a rejection and later deleted in reissue, the deletion would be presumed a broadening related to surrendered subject matter and barred unless materially narrowed related to surrendered subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Can Make the Surrendering Argument (applicant vs examiner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surrender of claimed subject matter cannot be based solely upon an applicant’s failure to respond to, or failure to challenge, an examiner’s statement made during prosecution; applicant is bound only by applicant’s amendments or positive arguments/statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's reasons for allowance alone cannot establish surrender. If applicant files comments supporting examiner's reasons, surrender may have occurred; if applicant files counter statements pointing to a different limitation as distinguishing, that different limitation may be the SGL. A general reply supporting allowance will not create surrender (Ex parte Yamaguchi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 — Material Narrowing Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the reissue claims were materially narrowed in other respects such that the surrendered subject matter is not entirely or substantially recaptured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reissue claims were materially narrowed relative to the surrendered subject matter (i.e., narrowing limitations relate to what was amended/argued in the original application), recapture may be avoided (Youman, Mostafazadeh). The reissue applicant should point out explicitly what limitation has been added to materially narrow and how it narrows the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation 1 — SGL Entirely Eliminated (recapture)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an SGL has been entirely eliminated from a reissue claim, then a recapture rejection under 35 U.S.C. 251 may be proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of an SGL, even if accompanied by other limitations making the claim narrower in unrelated aspects, is impermissible recapture (Pannu). A reissue claim that omits the surrender-generating limitation will generally be barred unless there is a new limitation related to the surrendered subject matter that materially narrows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation 2 — SGL Modified but Not Entirely Eliminated
rubrics_metrics.description: If an SGL has been retained but made less restrictive (broadened) in the reissue claim, determine whether the retained portion materially narrows the original claims to avoid recapture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the retained portion materially narrows relative to the surrendered subject matter, recapture may be avoided. If the retained portion is well known in the prior art or contained in prior art relied upon in original prosecution, it may not be materially narrowing and recapture exists (Mostafazadeh, Youman).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation 3 — Material Narrowing in Other Respects Must Relate to Surrendered Subject Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the SGL is eliminated or not materially narrowed, recapture can be avoided if the reissued claims were materially narrowed in other respects that relate to the surrendered subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrowing limitations unrelated to the surrendered subject matter are insufficient. The material narrowing must address what was amended or argued by applicant in the original application (Greenliant, Gen. Electric example). Applicant can rebut Office recapture finding by showing such related material narrowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparing Reissue Claims to Canceled Claims (recapture bar)
rubrics_metrics.description: The recapture rule bars the patentee from acquiring, through reissue, claims that are in all aspects the same scope as, or broader in scope than, those claims canceled from the original application to obtain a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reissue claims are narrower with respect to the added limitation that defined over the art (i.e., they retain the entirety of the limitation added in original prosecution), there will be no recapture even if the reissue claims are broader in some other, non-surrender-related aspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparing Reissue Claims to Patent Claims (four-part analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reissue claims are both broadened and narrowed versus the patent claims, examine whether the broadening is 'germane to a prior art rejection' (i.e., related to surrendered subject matter) and whether any narrowing is related to the surrender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reissue claims are broader by entirely omitting surrender-generating limitations and only narrowed in unrelated aspects, there is recapture. If reissue claims are narrower or equal in scope in the area related to surrendered subject matter and broader in unrelated aspects, there is no recapture (examples provided).
